Notes: First documented Jews in Lubartow; by end of 16th century a Jewish kahal existed
164 houses owned by Jews; community maintained two synagogues and a mikveh (source gives 1765 for houses)
approximately one third of total population per this source; other sources say about 3500 or 42%
November 1939: over 2500 Jews ordered to leave town and settle in Parczew and Ostrow (expulsion; not a count of remaining residents)
Autumn 1939 after expulsion only 818 Jews remained (Ostrow Lubelski 850 and Parczew 634 expelled there)
Ghetto: about 3500 Jews initially including 2000 from Slovakia; peak 4500; includes deportees so not resident count
Oct 11 1942 final deportation to Belzec/Sobibor (about 3000 per Wikipedia; source HHS says ~7000 from Lubartow and area) plus 300 murdered locally; deportation counts not population
Lubartow declared Judenfrei February 1943; only about 40 Jews survived the ghetto liquidation
